A weekend on the ridge

Two days, 31 km and one very windy summit. Here's the route, the gear and what we'd change.

By Sam Rivera · 8 min read · Updated this week

We left the trailhead just after sunrise, when the valley was still blue and the ridge above it was already gold. The first five kilometres climb steadily through pine forest, which is a gentle way to warm up before the switchbacks begin.

The route at a glance

Day 1 · Forest climb14 km · 980 m up
Night · Saddle campWater 200 m below
Day 2 · Ridge walk17 km · 620 m up

The saddle camp is exposed, so pitch low and stake everything twice. We filtered water from the spring on the north side, which was running well even late in the season.

Packing checklist

  • Wind shell and warm hat
  • 2 L water + filter
  • Stove, fuel and lighter
  • Headlamp with spare batteries
  • Offline map and paper backup

What we'd change

Start the ridge earlier. By noon the wind picked up enough that conversation was a shouting match, and the last exposed section is much more pleasant in calm morning air. We'd also carry a lighter tent: the extra comfort wasn't worth a kilo on the climb.

If you go, check the forecast for gusts, not just rain. The ridge is beautiful in clear weather and miserable in a storm.
